Shell_Pest_2025_Cliona

2025-10-13

To make things cleaner this is only code for Cliona Intensity and Prevalence. Clams and Polydora will be addressed in separate scripts.


~~~ Intensity: Initial GLMM Models ~~~ 

## === Counts: INITIAL MODEL COMMENTS === 
##       1. Basic data exploration showed that the best data distribution was a Beta distribution (continuous probability distributions defined on the interval [0, 1]) which subsets only non-zero data.
##       2. Thus this analysis examines only the 57% of individuals with some level of cliona infestation.
##       3. The analysis of those infected or not is captured in the Prevalence section below.
## 
## Model selection based on AICc:
## 
##                          K     AICc Delta_AICc AICcWt Cum.Wt      LL
## 7-TotalWeight+SH+Section 6 -4548.22       0.00      1      1 2280.13
## 4-Section+TotalWeight    5 -4533.39      14.83      0      1 2271.71
## 5-Section+SH             5 -4452.09      96.13      0      1 2231.06
## 1-SectionOnly            4 -4384.40     163.82      0      1 2196.21
## 6-TotalWeight+SH         4 -4384.36     163.86      0      1 2196.19
## 2-TotalWeightOnly        3 -4370.78     177.43      0      1 2188.40
## 3-ShellHeightOnly        3 -4318.03     230.19      0      1 2162.02
## === Intensity: INITIAL MODEL SELECTION INSIGHTS === 
##       1. Section is highly important (1 >> 2 or 3 alone), TotalWeight is more important than ShellHeight (2 >> 3).
##       2. The best model includes all three effects (7 >> 4 or 5 or 6).
##       3. The best model fit involved subsetting the data to exclude oysters with no Cliona. Including cliona-free oysters caused issues with residuals due to the large number of zeros in the data.
## The following is Residual results, QQ Plot, R2, and Summary for the best fitting model ONLY: 
##     7-TotalWeight+SH+Section

## Object of Class DHARMa with simulated residuals based on 250 simulations with refit = FALSE . See ?DHARMa::simulateResiduals for help. 
##  
## Scaled residual values: 0.624 0.648 0.232 0.092 0.788 0.78 0.676 0.32 0.092 0.612 0.736 0.668 0.232 0.3 0.8 0.884 0.384 0.852 0.34 0.008 ...

##  Family: beta  ( logit )
## Formula:          
## ClionaIntensityWholeOyster ~ TotalWeight_scaled + ShellHeight_scaled +  
##     Section
## Data: subset(ShellPest2, ClionaIntensityWholeOyster > 0)
## 
##       AIC       BIC    logLik -2*log(L)  df.resid 
##   -4548.3   -4513.3    2280.1   -4560.3      2497 
## 
## 
## Dispersion parameter for beta family (): 6.78 
## 
## Conditional model:
##                    Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)        -1.88830    0.04013  -47.05  < 2e-16 ***
## TotalWeight_scaled  0.35296    0.03366   10.49  < 2e-16 ***
## ShellHeight_scaled -0.14093    0.03452   -4.08 4.46e-05 ***
## SectionC           -0.20723    0.05705   -3.63 0.000281 ***
## SectionE            0.35840    0.04468    8.02 1.04e-15 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## === Intensity: INITIAL MODEL INSIGHTS ===
##   ClionaIntensityWholeOyster ~ TotalWeight_scaled + ShellHeight_scaled + Section
##       1. Model fits the data alright with decent residuals. KS and disperison tests indicate fit issues, though this is common with large data sets.
##       2. R-squared of 0.103 indicates a weak predictive ability, meaning there's lots of room for improvement.
##       3. Larger oysters have more a higher intensity of cliona This makes sense and conforms to basic observations.
##       4. Counterintuitively, oysters with a greater shell height show slightly less cliona at a given weight.
##       5. There are statistically significant differences in the cliona intensity observed in the sections of the Bay.

## === Intensity: BIAS TESTING IMPORTANCE TABLE & ICC ===
##       1. Adjusted ICC indicates that after controling for other factors, ~23% of the variance is attributable to the random effects. Thus it is not the main driver of total variation but it is meaningful, and much more than the fixed effects.
##       2. The small percent of total variance contributed by the random effects is an artifact of the Beta model and doesn't fully represent the importance of these effects. More important is the overall better fit (AIC) and an improved conditional R-squared (0.329 vs. 0.151). 
##       3. Large Positive ΔAIC indicates that TotalWeight and Season are important predictors. 
##       4. Section's negative ΔAIC indicates it doesn't really improve the model.
##       5. TotalWeight and Season by have very small p-values, indicating they are highly significant.
##       6. Year and ShellHeight are both significant with very low p-values but far less than weight and season.
##       7. Shell Height effects are weak, but statistically significant (p = 0.004)
##       8. Section is not significant (p = 0.153).
##       9. ΔR2 measures how much of the model’s explained variance is uniquely attributable to that predictor. Even the most important variables explain a tiny amount of variance (less than 2%).
##  |||||||||||||||||||||||||||| CONCLUSION |||||||||||||||||||||||||||| 
##     1. TotalWeight is by far the strongest driver of cliona intensity. Heavier oysters tend to have more cliona.
##     2. Given the outsized impact of bias on this data, no other strong insights can be drawn without significant reprocessing, retraining, and robust QA measures being put in place. After which all these tests need to be run again and more detailed analysis run to determine any significant differences.
##     3. This solution represents a large input of staff time (thousands of hours) for a small amount of benefit.
## *** 4. Recommendation is to discontinue measuring cliona intensity in ShellPest data. ***


~~~ Prevalence: Initial GLMM Models ~~~ 

## === Prevalence: INITIAL MODEL COMMENTS === 
##       1. Basic data exploration showed that the best data distribution was a binomial since this is binary data. 
##       2. Present = 1; Absent = 0

## === Prevalence: INITIAL MODEL SELECTION INSIGHTS ===

##       2. Section is highly important (1 >> 2 or 3)
##       3. Of the two, TotalWeight is more important than ShellHeight (2 > 3)

##       1. Model fits the data pretty well with good residuals and and R-squared much better than the Improved model (0.499 vs. 0.333). KS Test fail is expected with a large data set, and nothing looks wrong with the plot otherwise.
##       2. ACF series residuals series looks much better, exhibiting no significant autocorrelation, implying that the model has effectively captured the temporal dependencies.
##       3. Much of the differences between sections and years is no longer significant, which may be an artifact of the biases.
##       3. The MASSIVE increase in model performance with both biases raise a lot of doubt about the Improved Model's insights.

## === Prevalence: BIAS TESTING IMPORTANCE TABLE & ICC ===
##       1. Adjusted ICC indicates that after controling for other factors, ~61% of the variance is attributable to the random effect of FixedLocation and 4% to ProcessedBy, which is substantial.
##       2. The Check for Multicollinearity show that the model’s fixed effects are clean, independent, and interpretable. No red flags for collinearity.
##       3. Large Positive ΔAIC indicates that TotalWeight is an extremely important predictor. 
##       4. Section and Year's low ΔAIC indicates they doesn't improve the model much.
##       5. TotalWeight and Year have very small p-values, indicating they are highly significant.
##       6. Section is not significant (p = 0.067).
##       7. ΔR2 measures how much of the model’s explained variance is uniquely attributable to that predictor. TotalWeight explains ~4% on its own; Year and Season add less than 0.5%.
##  |||||||||||||||||||||||||||| CONCLUSION |||||||||||||||||||||||||||| 
##     1. TotalWeight is by far the strongest driver of cliona prevalence. Heavier oysters tend to have higher cliona prevalence.
##     2. Given the outsized impact of bias on this data, no other strong insights can be drawn without significant reprocessing, retraining, and robust QA measures being put in place. After which all these tests need to be run again and more detailed analysis run to determine any significant differences.
##     3. This solution represents a large input of staff time (thousands of hours) for a small amount of benefit.
## *** 4. Recommendation is to discontinue noting the presence or absence of cliona in ShellPest data. ***
